newsitem.title: INDIA: Patnaik, veteran Indian nationalist, dies at 81.
newsitem.headline: Patnaik, veteran Indian nationalist, dies at 81.

text.p: Veteran Indian nationalist Bijoyananda Patnaik, a leader of the caretaker centre-left coalition, died of heart and respiratory problems on Thursday, officials of his Janata Dal party said. He was 81.

Patnaik, a socialist leader with a flamboyant lifestyle and aristocratic family origins, fought for the independence of both India and Indonesia before becoming the chief minister of the eastern state of Orissa.
Known as "Biju", Patnaik began his political career as a member of the Congress party and senior aide of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
But he fell out with Nehru's daughter, Indira Gandhi, and spent time in jail as a political prisoner under her two-year emergency rule from 1975.
Patnaik had previously been jailed by the country's British rulers during India's fight for freedom which culminated in independence in August 1947.

Months after independence, as a qualified pilot, Patnaike flew the first Indian aircraft into the disputed Kashmir region, where India was fighting the first of what would be three wars with neighbouring Pakistan.
Indonesia awarded Patnaik the "Bhumiputra" (Son of the Soil) award for his help in 1948 in rescuing two independence fighters from Dutch soldiers by landing his plane in the middle of a paddy field.
In 1996, Indonesia awarded Patnaik its "Bintang Jasa Utama" award, the highest national honour.

Patnaik's death affected efforts by the defeated United Front coalition to choose a new leader to replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who lost a confidence motion in the lower house last Friday.
Patnaik was a senior leader of Deve Gowda's Janata Dal, the biggest single unit in the 15-party United Front coalition.

The alliance's decision-making Steering Committee had been expected to select a new leader at a meeting set for Thursday, but officials said the panel was likely to pass a resolution honouring Patnaik and later adjourn without taking a decision.
The United Front was now expected to elect a new leader on Friday, an alliance spokesman said.

On March 30, the Congress party withdrew support for Deve Gowda's 10-month-old coalition, which lost a confidence vote in parliament last week. But Congress agreed to renew support after the front said it would change leaders.
